# docs(upflow): one ADO guard is inert, and the 2-segment form is ambiguous

<!-- Generated by SessionEnd hook from a commit matching a journal-worthy pattern.
     Next session: review, then promote to a real journal entry OR delete. -->

**Commit**: `0c0fbcb39314` — docs(upflow): one ADO guard is inert, and the 2-segment form is ambiguous

**Body**:

Comment-only; verified no executable line changed. Both entries came from a
review lane that was hook-blocked before it could measure anything and handed
over its hypotheses instead — each is recorded here only after being measured.

1. THE `segs.length !== 3` GUARD IS NOT INDEPENDENTLY LOAD-BEARING.
   Relaxing it alone to `< 3` reds NOTHING; the suite stays 35/35. The reason
   is arithmetic: the downstream `segs.length !== 2` gate demands `n - 1 === 2`,
   i.e. `n === 3`, which is exactly what the earlier line enforces. So it is a
   defensive restatement, and a green suite under a mutation there is NOT
   evidence the ADO count is instrumented.

   Recorded because `instrument-discipline.md` MUST-2(b) says a non-reddening
   mutation leaves TWO live hypotheses — vacuous test or inert mutation — and
   without this note the next person to mutate that line would be entitled to
   record a vacuity verdict against a fixture that is fine. Resolved here as
   INERT, with the arithmetic that settles it. The honest mutation for ADO
   exactness is the PAIR, which is how the originating exploit was closed.

2. THE 2-SEGMENT ORG-SUBDOMAIN FORM IS GENUINELY AMBIGUOUS.
   ADO permits omitting the project segment when project and repository names
   match, so both of these filter to two segments and nothing in the string
   tells them apart:
     <org>.visualstudio.com/<project>/_git/<repo>     -> [project, repo]
     <org>.visualstudio.com/<collection>/_git/<repo>  -> [collection, repo]
   This code takes the first reading, so a project-omitted URL derives the
   COLLECTION as the project. Measured:
     .../DefaultCollection/_git/repo -> {project: "defaultcollection", ...}

   PRE-EXISTING — the old last-two rule produced the identical pair, so it is
   not a consequence of the collection allowance added in 6cf74fa. FAIL-CLOSED
   in effect: the wrong project mismatches the caller's `repoRef.project` and
   the completion is refused. But a wrong derivation that happens to refuse is
   not the same as a correct refusal, and the difference is visible to anyone
   reading a refusal reason naming a project they never used. Resolving it
   needs a signal outside the URL (an API lookup) that this module deliberately
   does not make.

Also measured and NOT a defect, recorded so it is not re-investigated:
`https://dev.azure.com/<org>/_git/<repo>` (project omitted, dev.azure.com form)
derives a generic owner/name pair with `ado: null` and is then refused by the
ADO adapter's `!selfAdo` branch — fail-closed, and unchanged by any fix on this
branch.

Gates unchanged: suite 35/35, differential 0 findings, disclosure clean.
